assembly_notes:
MULTIPLICITY roller_count.
N rollers on one pitched line, every one parented to the frame and none chained. CONTIGUOUS integer range 4..24, and the bounds come from the mechanism, the host capacity and the budget -- NOT from which integers the source pool happens to contain (AUTHORING 3). The source values 5, 8, 12, 18 and 24 are evidence that the rule holds at five separate scales; they are not the range.
RULE (index-general, and this is what licenses a contiguous range): 001 L110-L113 and L222 write x_i = (i - (N-1)/2) * pitch; 002 L209 and L234 write the algebraically identical first_x = -((N-1)*pitch)/2 then x_i = first_x + i*pitch. The SAME loop runs twice in 002 -- L209-L230 for the frame's fixed bearing inserts and L232-L276 for the roller parts and joints -- which is what keeps the fixed and moving halves co-indexed. Frame length closes in closed form too: Mode A gives FRAME_LENGTH = (N-1)*pitch + 0.190 exactly at N = 5, 8 and 18; Mode B gives pitch = (FRAME_LENGTH - 0.120)/N exactly at N = 24 and 12. Nothing in either rule has a term that only works at a sampled N.
LOWER BOUND 4 -- GEOMETRY. N is the station count, so there are N-1 inter-roller gaps. Below N=4 there are fewer than 3 gaps and no item can be handed from one supporting pair to the next without at some point resting on a single roller, which is the defining function of a roller bed rather than a roller table. N=3 also gives a Mode A frame of 0.330 m against a 0.580 m width -- 43 percent wider than long. The source's own minimum of 5 sits inside the range, so the evidence stays reachable, and reaching 4 costs one more term of the same rule.
UPPER BOUND 24 -- BUDGET, not provenance and not capacity. Capacity does not bind globally: the rule pitch >= 2r + 0.016 (001 L419-L427 asserts 0.016..0.020 per adjacent pair) is a per-config constraint that resolve_config enforces, and under Mode A the pitch is independent so it can always be raised. Under Mode B at the widest frame it would permit N near 55. What binds is cost, which grows linearly in N on three axes: parts N+1+4*stations, mandatory motion-QC poses 3N from the CONTINUOUS roller joints, and collision solids 69+8N (up to 69+13N for split_twin_half_roller). At N=24 the worst combination -- folding_hinged_legs at 3 stations -- is 37 parts / 36 joints, 72 mandatory roller poses and 381 collision solids. That is above the fleet's largest shipped object (33 parts / 32 joints, shelving_unit_with_adjustable_shelves) and roughly double the fleet p90 of 19 parts, but it is accepted here because it is not invented: var_support_folding_legs builds exactly that 37-part / 36-joint object at N=24 and asserts it at L408-L412. WHAT IS GIVEN UP by stopping at 24: the placement rule itself would carry much further, and a longer conveyor is a real object. Going higher would need (a) a leg-station rule for frames beyond 2.4 m, which the pool does not contain because 002 fixes three stations regardless of N, and (b) a pose budget that 3N does not blow -- at N=40 a seed would carry 120 mandatory roller poses over ~590 collision solids. Both are solvable, neither is solvable from this evidence, so 24 is a budget ceiling that happens to coincide with the largest attested value rather than being set by it.
N CHANGES NOTHING ELSE: all three count forks leave roller_radius_m, bed_height_m, frame_outer_width_m, roller_length_m, the rail sections and the leg/foot count alone. Per AUTHORING 4 N is raw_domain only and never inflates core.

IDENTITY: a grounded beam frame carrying N independently free-spinning rollers on a common transverse axis line, plus a floor-support structure under the frame. +X is the conveying direction, +Y is the roller spin axis, +Z is up and z=0 is the floor.

DOMAIN. core_domain = 4 frame_form x 5 support_form x 3 roller_form x 2 roller_layout = 120, and every one of those 120 must build -- TemplateDomain has no compatibility gates. raw_domain = 120 x 5 N values = 600. Palette, rail proportions, tick/groove detail and the leg station count count toward neither.

JOINT TYPE, AND ITS COST. Every roller joint in all twelve source records is REVOLUTE with symmetric limits (001 L243-L248 uses +-2pi, the whole 002 family L268-L273 uses +-pi). A free gravity roller has no travel limit, so the rebuild makes them CONTINUOUS. The cost is real and was priced before setting the N cap: AUTHORING 5 makes -90, +90 and 180 mandatory poses for every continuous joint on top of the global neutral, so a seed carries 3N required roller poses -- 15 at N=5 and 72 at N=24 -- each running full collision QC. Two consequences. (a) N is capped at 24, which is both the largest source value and the point where pose cost, the pitch-clearance ceiling (~29 under Mode B) and the absence of a leg-station rule for longer frames all agree. (b) 001's author check L369-L383 asserts limits.lower < 0 < limits.upper, which a continuous joint cannot satisfy; the rebuild's equivalent test asserts the axis, the parent and the origin instead. The foot PRISMATIC joints and the folding-leg REVOLUTE joints keep their source types and limits.

CROSS-SLOT RISKS, all resolved by derivation rather than by gating:
(a) THE RAIL-VS-CROWN FLIP. The two origins disagree in SIGN: 001's rail top is 11 mm BELOW the roller crown, 002's is 36 mm ABOVE it. rail_top_above_crown_m is a signed per-candidate parameter and rail_top_z_m derives from it, so no seed hard-codes either convention. Hard-coding one would bury half the fleet's rollers in the rails.
(b) THE FRAME-LENGTH MODE. Mode A (001 family) fixes pitch and grows the frame; Mode B (002) fixes the frame and spreads the pitch, because it carries three fixed leg stations; Mode C (the arc) derives length from radius x angle and spreads rollers across the full arc with zero end inset. frame_length_mode is a derived string that the pitch, the length and all four derived frame features read, so the choice is encoded rather than commented.
(c) THE CURVED SPIN AXIS. swept_curved_arc is the only candidate whose roller axis is not global +Y; it is the local radial direction per station. frame_spin_axis_expr carries that, and the axis interface takes an expression rather than a literal triple for exactly this reason. It combines with all 3 roller forms and all 5 supports; nothing is excluded.
(d) SCISSOR STANCE. scissor_crossed_base puts its feet 80 mm outboard of the rails, widening the frame AABB. That is why the plane interfaces carry real extents instead of the host bounding box -- leg_footprint_v_m spans the full stance for this candidate alone.

COLLISION BUDGET. sdk/_core/v0/exact_collisions.py:L94-L118 derives one collision solid per visual, 1:1, so N drives the budget directly. Measured from the source constructions: 84 solids at 001/N=8, 154 at N=18, 261 at 002/N=24, and 369 for split_twin_half_roller at N=24 -- the worst case, and the one most likely to strain the 12 s per-build preflight budget. Two mitigations, both source-grounded. First, the 002 family's per-station rail_fastener visual (L222-L230) is a 4 mm decorative screw head costing 2N collision solids -- 48 at N=24 -- and 001 has no such feature at all; the rebuild welds it into the web. Second, split_twin_half_roller's overlap fix replaces sleeve + two split rings + a frame spacer with a single bored sleeve, removing 3N solids as a side effect. Swept rails are NOT a cost: each is one mesh visual regardless of arc_path_samples.

CONNECTION OVERLAPS vs RUNNING CLEARANCES (MECHANICAL_PRIORS 1c). Exact tangency between solids is fragile -- CadQuery union can keep tangent solids separate, triangulation can open at the seam, and connectivity is checked at contact_tol=1e-6 -- so every zero-distance meeting in the pool had to be classified. The rule: anything that never moves gets a deliberate overlap, anything that moves keeps a real gap. WELDS (all intra-part, all authored at exactly 0 in the source): rail web to flanges (002 L142-L149, both 0.865), leg top to crossmember (L39-L41 vs L165, both 0.640), bearing insert outer face to rail inner face (L213-L221, both 0.3975), rail fastener to web (L222-L230, both 0.4425) -- these take structural_weld_embed_m or fitting_weld_embed_m. The idiom is source-attested: var_frame_form_expanding_straight L146-L148 already embeds its foot pad into the chord 'to ensure geometric connectivity' and var_frame_form_curved_arc L347 embeds its rail fastener 'for connection'. RUNNING FITS (unchanged, still real gaps): the axle end against the bearing insert, the frame ring against the roller end cap, the barrel against the rail (0.014 / 0.0555), adjacent rollers at pitch - 2r >= 0.016, the leveler jaw against the threaded stem, and the telescoping sleeve bore. The bearing insert is the one feature carrying BOTH: welded into the rail at its outer end, clear of the axle at its inner end. Sizing is scale-aware over the 0.470-2.400 m span and stays an order of magnitude below the strictest overlap gate (overlap_tol defaults to 1e-3, and fcl.collide is only consulted once AABB depth exceeds it on ALL THREE axes -- the contact normal is always the shallow axis for a face weld) while staying four orders above the 1e-6 connectivity tolerance. This category has NO rigid inter-part connection: the frame is the only root and every other part is joint-carried, so allow_isolated_part remains the support escape throughout, and no running fit was converted into an overlap.

ALLOWANCES. The source pool emits 96 allow_overlap calls across four records -- 24 unscoped part-pair calls in split_rollers (L487-L493), 48 in curved_arc (L530-L540), 12 in telescoping_legs (L498-L519) and 12 in scissor_base (L505-L525). Preflight BLOCKS every one of them for a Design-backed template. Neither origin needs any, and the replacement route is theirs: bore the solids that the forks left solid (sleeve_wall_m, sleeve_bore_r_m, bearing_bore_r_m), re-derive the curved bearing in the local radial frame instead of inflating it, and copy 002's tangent leveler-jaw capture (L71-L77, jaw inner face at exactly the stem radius) for the scissor foot plate. Where a member is then genuinely carried by its joint on a running clearance -- every roller, and the telescoping foot -- the seed declares ctx.allow_isolated_part, which preflight explicitly does not block. Zero allow_overlap in any emitted seed is a category anchor.

THREE SOURCE DEFECTS THE REBUILD CORRECTS. (1) scissor_crossed_base authors its pivot bolt and both flanges as Z-axis cylinders (L85-L98) although the arms lie in the YZ plane and the pin must run along X. (2) folding_hinged_legs places its pivot bolt at local z = -0.008 (L79-L84), 8 mm below the hinge axis its own joint declares at HINGE_Z. (3) pantograph_scissor_chords bottoms out at z = 0.015 rather than 0 (L150), so as authored it floats. All three are MECHANICAL_PRIORS 4 or grounding violations, corrected in the derived values rather than reproduced.

PART TREE. frame (root) -> N rollers in parallel; plus, per support candidate, either nothing (fixed_corner_plate_feet), 2*stations leveling feet on the frame, or 2*stations folding legs on the frame each carrying one foot -- the only depth-2 chain in the category. Seed part count runs from N+1 (corner plates, N=5 -> 6 parts) to N+1+4*stations (folding legs at N=24, 3 stations -> 37 parts, which is exactly what the source builds).

derived.expression: 'A' if frame_form in ('low_profile_extrusion_deck', 'pantograph_scissor_chords') else ('C' if frame_form == 'swept_curved_arc' else 'B')
derived.name: frame_length_mode
derived.rationale: Which frame-length strategy the candidate uses, carried as a derived value so the pitch, the frame length and every derived frame feature read one source of truth. Mode A is the 001 family: no legs, so the frame is free to grow. Mode B is 002: three fixed leg stations at LEG_XS (L29), so the frame must stay put and the pitch spreads instead. Mode C is the arc, where length is not authored at all. This is the choice the coordinator asked to be encoded rather than commented.

derived.expression: (roller_count - 1) * roller_pitch_m + 2.0 * end_inset_m if frame_length_mode == 'A' else (arc_radius_m * arc_angle_rad if frame_length_mode == 'C' else frame_length_authored_m)
derived.name: frame_length_m
derived.rationale: MODE A: FRAME_LENGTH = (N-1)*pitch + 0.190, exact at all three source points (4*0.070+0.190 = 0.470 at N=5, 7*0.070+0.190 = 0.680 at N=8, 17*0.070+0.190 = 1.380 at N=18), i.e. 0.095 per end. MODE C: the arc fork preserved centreline length exactly -- ARC_RADIUS * ARC_ANGLE = 3.0 * 0.80 = 2.400 = the straight parent's FRAME_LENGTH (002 L25) -- so length is derived from the two arc parameters rather than authored. MODE B: independent, see the candidate parameter.

derived.expression: roller_pitch_m if frame_length_mode == 'A' else (frame_length_m / (roller_count - 1) if frame_length_mode == 'C' else (frame_length_m - 0.120) / roller_count)
derived.name: station_pitch_m
derived.rationale: MODE B: pitch = (FRAME_LENGTH - 0.120)/N, exact at both source points (2.280/24 = 0.095 in origin 002, 2.280/12 = 0.190 in var_roller_count_12, which changes ONLY those two constants). MODE C differs and the SourceMap records why: the curved fork spreads rollers across the FULL arc with ZERO end inset (ROLLER_ANGLES L41-L44 runs -HALF_ARC..+HALF_ARC), giving a centreline pitch of arc_length/(N-1) = 2.400/23 = 0.10435 rather than Mode B's 0.095. Forcing Mode B onto the arc would silently move every station.

derived.name: station_span_m
derived.rationale: Centre-to-centre span of the roller bed, first station to last.

derived.name: station_x_m
derived.rationale: THE index-general station rule, verbatim from 001 L110-L113 and L222. 002 L209/L234 writes the algebraically identical first_x + i*pitch. Centred on x=0 in every record. 001 L332-L345 asserts |x_{i+1} - x_i - pitch| <= 1e-7 for every adjacent pair.

derived.name: station_delta_rad
derived.rationale: swept_curved_arc only: the angular station coordinate that replaces station_x_m and drives the per-roller radial spin axis. Source L41-L44.

derived.name: station_axis_z_m
derived.rationale: Per-station axis height. One helper feeds BOTH the frame's fixed bearing inserts and the roller joint origins, exactly as _roller_axis_z(i) does in var_roller_layout_staggered_rollers (defined L36-L38, called L224 for bearings and L250/L286 for joints). Computing them separately is how the fixed and moving halves drift apart.

derived.name: roller_gap_m
derived.rationale: HARD CONSTRAINT, asserted per adjacent pair in the source: 001 L419-L427 runs expect_gap(min_gap=0.016, max_gap=0.020) and the built value is 0.070 - 2*0.026 = 0.018. 002's margin is 0.095 - 0.068 = 0.027. The stagger term is why staggered_alternating_height RELAXES this rule instead of tightening it: centre distance becomes sqrt(0.095^2 + 0.025^2) = 0.0982 rather than 0.095. resolve_config must reject any combination with roller_gap_m < 0.016.

derived.name: frame_end_crossmember_x_m
derived.rationale: Derived frame feature 1. var_roller_count_5 L64-L72 generalises 001's magic +-0.315 to ROLLER_SPAN_HALF + 0.070. Checks out at N=8 (0.245+0.070 = 0.315) and N=18 (0.595+0.070 = 0.665).

derived.name: frame_corner_plate_x_m
derived.rationale: Derived frame feature 2. var_roller_count_5 L84-L86: plate_x = FRAME_HALF - 0.015. Checks out at N=8 (0.340-0.015 = 0.325) and N=18 (0.690-0.015 = 0.675). The same x also carries the recessed plate screws (L127).

derived.name: frame_groove_length_m
derived.rationale: Derived frame feature 3. var_roller_count_5 L102-L109: groove_length = FRAME_LENGTH - 0.070. Checks out at N=8 (0.610) and N=18 (1.310).

derived.name: frame_cross_brace_x_m
derived.rationale: Derived frame feature 4, and the one place the three count forks DISAGREE: var_roller_count_5 L74-L82 uses 1.5*pitch (0.105), origin 001 uses 2.5*pitch (0.175) and var_roller_count_18 uses 5*pitch (0.350). All three are within 3 percent of FRAME_LENGTH/4 (0.1175 / 0.170 / 0.345), which is the only rule that keeps the braces inboard at every N, so that is what the rebuild uses.

derived.name: rail_centre_y_m
derived.rationale: Centreline of each side rail. 001 L48: +-0.2725. 002 L28 RAIL_CENTER_Y: +-0.420.

derived.name: rail_inner_y_m
derived.rationale: Inner face of the side rail -- the datum the WHOLE axial chain hangs off. 001: 0.2725 - 0.0175 = 0.255, which the source names RAIL_INNER_Y at L29. 002: 0.420 - 0.0225 = 0.3975.

derived.name: roller_half_length_m
derived.rationale: Half the barrel length. 001: 0.241. 002: 0.342.

derived.name: barrel_axial_clearance_m
derived.rationale: Clear air between the barrel end face and the rail inner face. 001: 0.014. 002: 0.0555. MECHANICAL_PRIORS 4 requires the frame to give REAL axial clearance rather than embedding the roller in the rail, and both origins do.

derived.name: end_cap_axial_clearance_m
derived.rationale: Clear air between the end cap outer face and the rail. 001: 0.255-0.247 = 0.008. 002: 0.3975-0.360 = 0.0375. Must stay positive at every parameter extreme.

derived.name: structural_weld_embed_m
derived.rationale: CONNECTION OVERLAP for heavy frame members welded to each other -- rail web to flanges, leg tube to crossmember, chord to pad, scissor arm to gusset. MECHANICAL_PRIORS 1c: exact tangency between solids is FRAGILE, because CadQuery union can keep tangent solids separate, triangulation can open at the seam, and find_part_geometry_connectivity_findings uses contact_tol=1e-6. Every one of those joins is authored at EXACTLY zero in the source -- 002's web top 0.865 = flange bottom 0.865 (L142-L149), leg top 0.640 = crossmember bottom 0.640 (L39-L41 vs L165) -- so every one needs a deliberate embed instead. Scale-aware because the pool spans 0.470 m to 2.400 m: 0.3 mm on the desk section, 0.6 mm on the floor unit, clamped to 1.0 mm. The idiom is source-attested, not invented: var_frame_form_expanding_straight L146-L148 comments 'Foot top face embeds slightly into the bottom chord to ensure geometric connectivity' and var_frame_form_curved_arc L347 embeds the rail fastener 'deeply into web for connection'.

derived.name: fitting_weld_embed_m
derived.rationale: CONNECTION OVERLAP for small fittings welded onto a rail -- bearing inserts, rail fasteners, leveler jaws, bolt flanges, pivot pins. Smaller than the structural weld because the features are smaller: 001's whole bearing ring is only 8 mm long (L36), so a 0.5 mm embed would be 6 percent of the part. 0.2-0.36 mm across the scale range. Both weld parameters stay an order of magnitude BELOW the strictest overlap gate (find_geometry_overlaps defaults to overlap_tol=1e-3, and it only calls fcl.collide when the AABB depth exceeds the tolerance on ALL THREE axes -- the contact normal is always the shallow axis here, so a sub-millimetre weld is filtered out before fcl is ever consulted) and four orders ABOVE the 1e-6 connectivity tolerance they exist to satisfy.

derived.name: interpart_connection_policy
derived.rationale: IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE. Both weld parameters above are INTRA-PART: every site they apply to is a frame visual meeting another frame visual, which the overlap gate never compares at all (collision is computed between parts). This category has NO rigid inter-part connection to overlap -- the frame is the only root, and every other part (rollers, leveling feet, folding legs) is attached by a joint and moves relative to it. So every cross-part meeting here is a RUNNING FIT and keeps a real clearance, with ctx.allow_isolated_part as the support escape. Converting a running fit into an overlap would be the opposite of the fix.

derived.name: bearing_insert_length_m
derived.rationale: THE central derivation of the category, and it now spans TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF INTERFACE -- one at each end, with opposite signs. The outer end is welded INTO the rail by fitting_weld_embed_m (intra-part, per 1c). The inner end holds running_clearance_m off the rotating axle (inter-part running fit, which must stay a gap). The insert is NOT a chosen length, it is the solved gap between the axle end face and the rail inner face. It holds in BOTH origins exactly, which the SourceMap only claimed for 002: 002 gives 0.3975 - 0.3825 = 0.015, the authored insert length at L213; 001 gives 0.255 - 0.247 = 0.008, the authored ring extrude height at L36. Two independent records, two scales, one formula. The running_clearance_m term is the rebuild's only addition, replacing a distance of exactly 0.

derived.name: bearing_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: Bore of the frame bearing insert. 001 authors this as a genuine ANNULUS (_bearing_ring_mesh L32-L41: outer 0.019, bore 0.0085 around a 0.006 axle = 2.5 mm radial clearance) which is why its axle can stop at the ring face without intersecting it. The rebuild uses the annular construction for every frame candidate.

derived.name: frame_spin_axis_expr
derived.rationale: MECHANICAL_PRIORS 4/5: the spin axis must pass through the roller centre and be coaxial with the axle. Straight frames use global +Y; swept_curved_arc uses the LOCAL RADIAL direction per station (L391-L398), which is the only axis change in the pool. A template that hard-codes (0,1,0) would spin every curved roller about a chord instead of its own axle.

derived.name: split_sleeve_bore_clearance_m
derived.rationale: split_twin_half_roller only, and the constraint that replaces its 24 unscoped allow_overlap calls (L487-L493). With the axle owned by the FRAME, the roller's central sleeve must be a real bore around it rather than the source's solid r=0.032 cylinder (L292-L300). resolve_config must reject any combination where this goes non-positive; that is what makes the allowance unnecessary instead of merely undeclared.

derived.name: roller_support_policy
derived.rationale: Both origins assert contact at distance EXACTLY 0 (001 contact_tol 0.0008 at L384-L389, 002 contact_tol 0.0002 at L384-L395), and fcl.collide treats 0 as a collision. The roller is supported kinematically by its joint, so the rebuild holds running_clearance_m and declares ctx.allow_isolated_part on each roller. That call is explicitly NOT blocked by preflight, unlike allow_overlap.

derived.name: bed_plane_z_m
derived.rationale: The conveying plane -- the crown of the rollers, where cargo actually rides. 001: 0.200+0.026 = 0.226. 002: 0.820+0.034 = 0.854.

derived.name: rail_top_z_m
derived.rationale: THE RAIL-VS-CROWN FLIP, and the reason rail_top_above_crown_m is signed. The pool contains BOTH conventions and they are opposite: 001's upper rail top is 0.215 against a 0.226 crown, so the conveying plane sits 11 mm ABOVE the rails; 002's top flange top is 0.890 against a 0.854 crown, so the rails stand 36 mm ABOVE the bed and act as guide rails. pantograph_scissor_chords inherits 001's sign at 4 mm; swept_curved_arc inherits 002's. A template that hard-codes either one buries half its seeds' rollers in the rails or leaves the other half unguided, so this MUST be derived per frame candidate.

derived.name: rail_guard_height_m
derived.rationale: How much rail stands proud of the cargo plane. Zero for the 001 family by construction; positive for the 002 family, where it is the guide function.

derived.name: bed_clear_width_m
derived.rationale: Clear width between rail inner faces -- the real cargo footprint, and the extent written into roller_bed_plane. Deliberately NOT the frame AABB width, which includes feet standing outboard (scissor_crossed_base puts them 80 mm outside the rails).

derived.name: roller_containment_margin_m
derived.rationale: 002 L396-L409 asserts expect_within(roller, frame, axes='xy', margin=0.0) for the first and last roller: the roller must lie inside the frame in plan. This margin is that check made constructive.

derived.name: support_mount_z_m
derived.rationale: Underside of the crossmember the legs abut. 002: crossmember spans 0.640..0.700 (L165) and the leg tube spans 0.120..0.640 (L39-L41), so leg top = crossmember bottom exactly, face to face with no overlap. Every plane in the leg chain is derived from this one.

derived.expression: top_flange_h_m + web_height_m + bottom_flange_h_m if frame_form in ('deep_channel_rail_bed', 'swept_curved_arc') else (chord_height_m if frame_form == 'pantograph_scissor_chords' else upper_rail_height_m + lower_rail_height_m)
derived.name: rail_stack_height_m
derived.rationale: Total rail section depth, per frame candidate. The 002 channel is 0.025+0.150+0.015 = 0.190 with faces abutting exactly; 001 stacks two separate extrusions; the pantograph has only a thin chord.

derived.name: leg_station_x_m
derived.rationale: Support stations spread symmetrically over the middle 75 percent of the frame. 002 L29 authors LEG_XS = (-0.900, 0, 0.900) on a 2.400 m frame, i.e. +-0.375 of the length, which this reproduces at leg_station_count = 3. Generalised because leg_station_count is a parameter and the frame length now moves with N under Mode A.

derived.name: leg_station_y_m
derived.rationale: Legs sit under the rail centreline in every candidate EXCEPT the scissor base, whose feet splay outboard to foot_stance_y_m (L30: 0.500 against a 0.420 rail). The scissor arms still MEET the frame at rail_centre_y_m -- that is the crossing geometry -- but the floor contact is outboard, which widens the frame AABB.

derived.expression: leg_outer_m if support_form in ('square_tube_legs_leveling_feet', 'folding_hinged_legs') else (2.0 * collar_r_m if support_form == 'telescoping_sleeve_legs' else (scissor_arm_thickness_m if support_form == 'scissor_crossed_base' else corner_plate_t_m))
derived.name: leg_footprint_u_m
derived.rationale: REAL mount footprint in X, per MECHANICAL_PRIORS 2 -- the actual carrying area, never the host AABB. The telescoping candidate's is set by its 0.070 mount plate (L69-L73), which is why it is the widest.

derived.expression: leg_outer_m if support_form in ('square_tube_legs_leveling_feet', 'folding_hinged_legs') else (2.0 * collar_r_m if support_form == 'telescoping_sleeve_legs' else (2.0 * foot_stance_y_m if support_form == 'scissor_crossed_base' else corner_plate_h_m))
derived.name: leg_footprint_v_m
derived.rationale: REAL mount footprint in Y. The scissor base spans the full stance because its arms cross the whole width, which is exactly the difference a plane extent is supposed to expose to mate_planes.

derived.expression: 'none' if support_form == 'fixed_corner_plate_feet' else ('revolute_legs_prismatic_feet' if support_form == 'folding_hinged_legs' else 'prismatic_feet')
derived.name: support_joint_topology
derived.rationale: How many extra joints the support slot contributes. fixed_corner_plate_feet contributes NONE -- the whole object is then N roller joints and nothing else, which is the source's own topology for 001 and is a legitimate seed.

derived.name: foot_part_count
derived.rationale: Two feet per station. 002 L347 asserts exactly 6 for its three stations.

derived.name: folding_leg_part_count
derived.rationale: folding_hinged_legs is the ONLY candidate that promotes the leg from frame geometry to a part, and therefore the only depth-2 chain in the pool: frame -> folding_leg_i -> leveling_foot_i (L378-L394 re-parents the foot joint).

derived.name: leg_head_engagement_z_m
derived.rationale: Top of the leg after welding. The source authors leg top = crossmember bottom = 0.640 EXACTLY (002 L39-L41 against L165), which 1c now identifies as the fragile construction: the leg is frame geometry, so a tangent seam can split the frame into two connectivity islands. derived.name: leg_bottom_z_m
